title: Proper direct image of unbounded complexes
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be schemes, $\ell$ a prime, $\Qlb$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $E\subseteq\Qlb$ a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, understood as the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] or [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], respectively. For $T=X,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and let $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ be the unbounded derived category of sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules, with cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\IndCons(T,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of sheaves isomorphic to filtered colimits, in $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$, of constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and define
$$
\Dic(T,\Lambda)=\{K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda):\mathcal H^n(K)\in\IndCons(T,\Lambda)\text{ for every }n\in\mathbf Z\}.
$$
Let $p:X\to Y$ be proper and let $d\in\mathbf Z$ bound the dimensions of all geometric fibres of $p$, as in [sk-lem-proper-heart-bound]. Let $Rp_*$ denote the total right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] of the module pushforward [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. For integers $a,b$, write $\Dic^{\leq b}(T,\Lambda)$ and $\Dic^{\geq a}(T,\Lambda)$ for the objects of $\Dic(T,\Lambda)$ whose cohomology vanishes in degrees $>b$, respectively $<a$. Use the canonical truncations of [def-kun-truncations]. Then $Rp_*$ maps $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$, and
$$
Rp_*\bigl(\Dic^{\leq b}(X,\Lambda)\bigr)\subset\Dic^{\leq b+2d+1}(Y,\Lambda),\qquad
Rp_*\bigl(\Dic^{\geq a}(X,\Lambda)\bigr)\subset\Dic^{\geq a}(Y,\Lambda).
$$
Moreover, for $K\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical truncation maps
$K\leftarrow\tau_{\leq q}K\to\tau_{\geq q-2d-1}\tau_{\leq q}K$ induce an isomorphism in $\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$
$$
\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)\simeq\mathcal H^q\bigl(Rp_*\tau_{\geq q-2d-1}\tau_{\leq q}K\bigr).
$$

external.place: An eventually constant tower has vanishing $\varprojlim^1$, so the Milnor sequence of [sk-prop-pe-milnor] gives $$ \mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)\simeq\mathcal H^q(Rp_*\tau_{\geq-n}K)\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }n. $$ The right side is covered by the bounded-below case.

proof.text: Clause (2) of [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums] states that both $\tau_{\leq r}K$ and $\tau_{\geq r}K$ remain in $\Dic$ whenever $K\in\Dic$. Its coefficients are exactly $E$ or $\Qlb$, so it applies to the present category. The good-truncation formulas in [def-kun-truncations] give $\mathcal H^j(\tau_{\geq r}K)=\mathcal H^j(K)$ for $j\geq r$ and zero otherwise, and the analogous formula for $\tau_{\leq s}K$. Thus $K_n=\tau_{\geq-n}K$ is bounded below, remains in $\Dic$, and has cohomology in degrees $\leq b$ whenever $K$ does. The same stability clause applies successively to both truncations used in the final window.

source.place: Bounded-below and arbitrary paragraphs: justify the truncations used in the reduction

proof.text: For bounded-below $L\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ apply [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below]. Its hypotheses are precisely our coefficients, proper $p$, and fibre-dimension bound $d$, together with boundedness below of $L$. It gives ind-constructible cohomology of $Rp_*L$ in every degree, the lower bound $a$ if $L\in\Dic^{\geq a}$, and the upper bound $b+2d+1$ if also $L\in\Dic^{\leq b}$. This invokes the existing bounded-below spectral-sequence node rather than using an uncited spectral sequence or an uncited closure theorem.

Fix arbitrary $K\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ and an integer $q$. The stabilization assertion of [det-proper-unbounded-window-arbitrary] supplies $N$ such that, for $n\geq N$, the canonical map $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)\to\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K_n)$ is an isomorphism. Choose also $n\geq0$. By step 1, $K_n$ is bounded below in $\Dic$, so [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below] makes the right-hand sheaf ind-constructible. Since $\IndCons$ was defined up to sheaf isomorphism, the left-hand sheaf is ind-constructible as well. Doing this separately for every $q$ proves $Rp_*K\in\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$. If $K\in\Dic^{\leq b}$, step 1 gives the same upper bound on $K_n$; the bounded-below node then makes the right-hand side zero for $q>b+2d+1$, and the canonical isomorphism makes the left-hand side zero. This proves the upper amplitude bound without imposing boundedness below on $K$.

source.place: Second paragraph, eventual-value isomorphism and its ind-constructibility and upper-bound consequences

proof.text: If $K\in\Dic^{\geq a}(X,\Lambda)$, then $K$ is already bounded below. The lower-bound assertion of [det-proper-unbounded-window-bounded-below] applies directly and gives $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)=0$ for $q<a$, together with ind-constructible cohomology. Hence $Rp_*K\in\Dic^{\geq a}(Y,\Lambda)$.

source.place: End of second paragraph, lower amplitude bound

proof.text: Put $A=\tau_{\leq q}K$ and $B=\tau_{\geq q-2d-1}A$. Step 1 gives $A,B\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$, and step 3 puts $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)$, $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*A)$ and $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*B)$ in $\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$. Apply [det-proper-unbounded-window-iso], with the same $\Lambda,p,d,K,q$: its statement says that the two canonical maps give isomorphisms $\alpha:\mathcal H^q(Rp_*A)\to\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)$ and $\beta:\mathcal H^q(Rp_*A)\to\mathcal H^q(Rp_*B)$. The required isomorphism is $\beta\circ\alpha^{-1}$, whose inverse is $\alpha\circ\beta^{-1}$; their composites are identities by cancellation. Since $\IndCons$ is a full subcategory of module sheaves, these maps and their inverses are morphisms in $\IndCons$. Thus this is exactly the isomorphism induced by the specified truncation zig-zag, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of its endpoints.
